_: The pack schema, with invented people. games.json beside this file is the real one.
_why_not_committed: No longer true, and kept as a warning: a pack used to carry rosters inline, which is why it was held out of the repository. A team now names a `roster` URL and the browser fetches the squad when the game is loaded, so a pack holds no personal data and games.json is committed. Inline `players` is for invented people only - put real ones there and the file stops being publishable.

_schema.video: YouTube id. Training mode stamps events with VIDEO time, so captures from different people align exactly.
_schema.teams: Two, in the order they should appear. `side` is O or D and only sets which group a player starts in; which side is on offence follows the point.
_schema.score: The tournament's own final score, if known. Not used to fill anything in - it is checked against what the capture recorded, and a disagreement means goals were missed.
_schema.roster: Per team, and the reason a pack needs no names in it. A URL returning {"players":[{player_id, firstname, lastname, num}]} - Live! publishes one per team under live/data/ and serves it with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the browser reads it directly on 'Load squads and video' and nothing is stored. `player_id` is the key shared/notes.php files matchings under, so a fetched squad can inherit them. Inline `players` still works, for invented people.
_schema.links: Where the tournament's own record lives: whatever statistics the event published, to compare a finished capture against, and per team the roster, to settle a shirt number the footage will not show. Put a link on the game when it is about the game and on the team when it is about the team - a team's link is shown under its own name, so two rosters do not both read 'roster'. Any number of either, in the order a spotter would reach for them. Opened in a new tab - nothing is fetched and nothing is stored.
_schema.division: Optional. Only read to decide whether the game is mixed, and so whether matchings are worth showing; the game's own name is used when this is absent, which is usually enough.
_schema.matching: MMP or FMP, per player. Nothing upstream records it - not shared/roster.php and not UltiOrganizer - so a mixed game has to be told here. It is what lets a called line be checked against the point's prescribed ratio; see shared/ratio.js and MATCHCONTROL.md section 10a. Leave it out outside mixed, where there is no ratio and nothing to check.
